claims.text: The rider's own claim measures the trip at 14.84 km against a booked optimal of 14.0 km, and the platform's own trace confirms it: trace_distance_km is 14.84 km, an excess of 0.84 km. Under POL-RD-01 the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.8 km, and the trace figure is the one that must be used for the threshold test.

The excess is 0.84 km, which is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold set by POL-RD-01, so the absolute limb of the establishment test passes. The rider's claim is not a rounding artefact: the trace itself, at 14.84 km, clears the 0.8 km gate by 0.04 km.

The percentage limb of POL-RD-01 fails and I concede it: the excess of 0.84 km is 6.00% of the 14.0 km optimal, well below the 20% threshold. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass, so on the trace as measured no route deviation is ESTABLISHED and the outcome on the deviation claim is NO_ACTION. I do not stretch this point.

The driver's only explanation is 'I followed the navigation', and the bundle contains no traffic advisory at all: EV-ADVIS-02806-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion cannot be tested against any advisory, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The absence itself is citable, and it is cited here.

The fare ledger shows no billing-integrity defect that would give the rider a standalone correction: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, airport_surcharge is 0.0, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom gantry line and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4).

The rider's profile does not trigger the corroboration uplift in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the special corroboration requirement for a claim with excess below 30% does not apply. This is the only profile field on the rider side that may ground a finding, and it does not help the rider here.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 0, far below the 3-or-more gate, and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 230 is 0.00, far below the 0.05 ratio gate. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags of 1 is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. No POL-RD-06 uplift or referral is available on this record.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 117 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and the trace is not impaired. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied because trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02806 and the pickup timestamp 2026-09-11T17:19:44+08:00 matches across the trace and the trip record.

The rider's claim that the fare was 'higher than normal' is not supported on the money side: the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is 20.3920 against a charged_total of 21.10, a refund of only 0.7080, which is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor only in the sense that it is a trivial sum and the deviation itself is not established. No POL-RD-02 refund runs because POL-RD-01 fails.

The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: the deviation fails the POL-RD-01 percentage test, no exculpatory clause is needed because no deviation is established, and no billing-integrity correction is available. The outcome on this rider-filed dispute is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03, which leaves the CHARGED payment status and the zero refund_issued_sgd as they are.

Under POL-RD-01 the establishment test requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The percentage limb fails outright (6.00% is far below 20%), and the absolute limb fails too (0.84 km is not greater than 0.8 km — it is 0.04 km over the line only if one misreads the test as 'at least'). Both tests must pass; neither does. No deviation exists on this trip's own numbers, and the rider's characterisation of the trip cannot change that.

The trace itself is clean and unimpaired, so there is no data failure to excuse the rider's claim. The GPS artifact carries 117 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, and the admissibility pre-pass tags it COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are not met on any of them, so the trace governs the threshold test at full weight and the rider cannot fall back on POL-RD-07(iii) or POL-RD-10(3) to send this to a human reviewer.

The driver's explanation — 'I followed the navigation' — is consistent with the trace and needs no exculpatory clause to survive, because there is nothing to excuse. The derived deviation status is recorded as 'no deviation', and the driver's track shows a single continuous run from 17:19:44 to 17:39:04 with no gaps and no unexplained stop. Where no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, and the driver keeps the fare as charged.

The fare ledger confirms the charge is intact and no refund has been issued: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 on a total_charged of 21.10. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves that present state exactly as it stands — the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence, so the charge remains in place and the driver is not out of pocket. This is the party-relative reading of NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute.

The rider's assertion of an external traffic cause is not on the record and cannot be run: the only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02806-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, and its issue detail records that no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be performed, so no closure-adjusted optimal exists and no excess is exonerated — but equally, no excess was ever established, so the missing advisory changes nothing on this record. The absence is citable and it cuts against any traffic excuse, not against the driver's clean trace.

The rider's profile does not support a corroboration demand against the driver, and the driver's profile does not support an adverse finding either. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 230, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more) is not met and no repeat-deviation finding or conduct referral is available. Both profiles are context only under POL-GEN-01 and neither moves the outcome.

The fare arithmetic is internally consistent and shows no billing-integrity defect that would survive independently of the deviation question. The ledger reconciles to total_charged of 21.10 with zero ERP lines, zero airport surcharge, zero tolls and a surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, and the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is 20.3920 — a difference of 0.7080, which is below the 0.50 de minimis only in the sense that it is above it, but the refund route is closed because no deviation was established in the first place. No phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge appears, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the charge of S$21.10 stands and the disputed S$2.00 is not refunded.

Distance test (POL-RD-01). The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02806) measures the trip at 14.84 km; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02806) is 14.0 km. I have used the trace figure of 14.84 km, as POL-RD-01 requires, and not the rounded 14.8 km convenience copy on the trip record. The excess is 0.84 km, which is 6.00% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The 0.84 km does clear the 0.8 km absolute gate by 0.04 km, but 6.00% is far below the 20% gate, so the establishment test fails and no route deviation exists on this trip. Both advocates reached this same conclusion and I accept it.

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 117 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gap longer than 90 seconds and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. It is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0 in the pre-pass. The trace therefore governs the threshold test at full weight, and no impairment escalation arises.

Traffic excuse and the missing advisory (POL-RD-13). The driver's statement that he followed the navigation was not tested against a traffic advisory, because the only advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-02806-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with no payload. POL-RD-13 provides that a traffic cause asserted for a measured deviation cannot be run without an advisory on file, and any such assertion carries no weight; but no deviation was measured here, so this changes nothing. The two discarded claims that cited the missing advisory are recorded in the audit below and were discarded by the referee for not naming its issue code.

Billing integrity (POL-RD-09). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02806) reconciles to a charged total of 21.10, with zero ERP gantries, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge and a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown. No phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge appears, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral is produced.

Profiles (POL-GEN-01). Both profiles are context only and none of their citable counters helps either side: the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration test is not triggered; the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 of 230 completed trips, so the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern (and its conduct referral) is not available. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and was correctly not substituted.

Outcome. With no deviation established, the rider's claim that the fare was higher than normal is not made out on the money side either: the optimal-route recomputation would be 20.3920 against 21.10, but POL-RD-02 never runs because POL-RD-01 fails. Under POL-GEN-03 the result is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.0. There is no monetary effect, so no execution-threshold question arises. The rider may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
Both briefs converge on the same numbers, and so do I.

THE THRESHOLD (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 14.84 km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.8 km. Against the booked optimal of 14.0 km the excess is 0.84 km, or 6.00%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to pass BOTH gates: more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of the optimal. The absolute gate is met (0.84 > 0.8), but the percentage gate is not (6.00% against 20%), and both must pass. No route deviation is established, whatever the rider's characterisation of the trip. The driver's assertion that 0.84 km does not exceed 0.8 km is arithmetically wrong (it does), but it changes nothing, because the percentage limb fails independently; the rider's concession on the percentage limb is correct.

THE TRACE IS CLEAN. EV-GPS-02806 carries 117 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, and the pre-pass tags it COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, it governs at full weight, and no corroboration or escalation on that ground arises.

WHAT FOLLOWS (POL-GEN-03). The outcome is NO_ACTION: the fare breakdown shows the trip CHARGED at 21.10 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and that present state stands. The ledger reconciles: base 3.80 + distance 11.10 + time 5.40 + platform fee 0.80 = 21.10, surge_multiplier 1.0 read off the fare_breakdown, zero ERP lines and no airport surcharge. The recomputed fare on the optimal route is 20.3920, a difference of 0.7080, but POL-RD-02's refund route opens only where POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation, and it does not. No phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge exist, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct and produces no billing-integrity referral.

THE PROFILES. Neither profile moves the outcome, and both advocates used only the citable counters. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d = 0, so POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift does not apply. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 230, so POL-RD-06's pattern test is not met — no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The mention of driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01; it was not used as a ground and decides nothing.

THE MISSING ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-02806-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0. It is not reached: the driver asserted no external traffic cause — 'I followed the navigation' is a denial, not a queue, closure or incident — so POL-RD-03 was never engaged, POL-RD-13 does not fire, and the absence of an advisory the driver never cited is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

NO ESCALATION. POL-RD-10 does not trigger: confidence is well above the 0.70 floor on artifacts of weight 1.0, the trip identifiers and pickup timestamp match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing cited artifact, the refund is zero, and every charge line reconciles.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-02806, and the outcome is that the fare as charged stands. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02806), which records trace_distance_km of 14.84 km against the booked optimal route of 14.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02806) — an excess of 0.84 km, or 6.00%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km; both limbs must pass. The percentage limb fails clearly (6.00% against a 20% threshold), so no deviation is established, and the absolute limb (0.84 km, just above the 0.8 km gate) cannot carry the test on its own. The rider's characterisation of the trip cannot change this arithmetic.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is owed. For transparency, the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is 20.3920 against a charged total of 21.10 (a difference of 0.7080), but that figure is not payable on this record. The driver's explanation, 'I followed the navigation', is consistent with the trace and required no exculpatory clause.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 117 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not met and the trace governs the threshold test at full weight. There is no impaired-trace escalation here and no fallback to POL-RD-07(iii) or POL-RD-10(3).

On billing integrity, the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02806) shows no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom line and nothing to correct under POL-RD-09(4). No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged.

Both profiles are context only under POL-GEN-01 and neither moves the outcome. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d = 0, substantiated = 0) does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement, and the driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags (0 against 230 completed trips) do not establish a repeat pattern under POL-RD-06, so no uplift or conduct referral is available. A mention in one claim of the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was correctly flagged as context-only and was not used as a ground.

No traffic advisory was on file (EV-ADVIS-02806-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), but no party cited an advisory identifier as an excuse, so nothing turns on its absence under POL-RD-13. Two claims in the record did cite the missing advisory without disclosing its issue code and were discarded by the referee; they appear in the discarded-claims list below.

The present state stands as it is: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The monetary effect of this ruling is nil, below the automatic-execution threshold, and the case carries no clause-mandated referral.
